inclusion_rule: Word or command classification studies whose ledger names a wearable non-acoustic sensor on the face or neck (strain, piezo or triboelectric sensor, surface EMG, accelerometer); the design compared is how test samples are separated from training samples: speaker-disjoint, session- or day-disjoint, or a random or per-class sample split. Boundary: a paper counts under every split it reports; reviews and acoustic-only studies are excluded when read.

candidates.snippet: Added by the reader: subject-specific models; leave-one-batch-out within sessions and leave-one-session-out after repositioning; no speaker-disjoint test.

read_fulltext.quote: we performed five-fold cross-validation tests with randomly mixed datasets
All recordings were made on one subject during one sitting to ensure that sensor position remained constant.
we employed a stratified 5-fold cross-validation scheme under a subject-independent setting
achieving leave-one-session-out accuracies of 64±18% and 54±7% for the vocalized and silent experiments, respectively.
The performance drops to 76.2% after repositioning the electrodes if no normalization or adaptation is performed.
Across all models, held-out test accuracy consistently exceeded the CV score, indicating that the test sets
accuracies of 71.1±8.3% and 59.3±2.2% for vocalized and silent speech, respectively.
